headline: AI Boosts Homework Scores by 18%, But Exams Plummet 20%, Study Finds
summary: A new study reveals students using AI tools saw homework grades rise significantly, yet their exam performance dropped sharply when AI was removed.
details: A six-month study tracking 27,000 students in China found that those who used AI tools like Doubao and DeepSeek saw their homework scores increase by 18% across all subjects.
However, when these same students were tested in exams without AI assistance, their scores fell by 20% compared to classmates who did not use AI.
The research, conducted by academics from Stockholm University and the University of Hong Kong, highlights a potential disconnect between AI-assisted task completion and genuine learning.

This aligns with concerns from educators who have noted a rise in formulaic essays suspected to be AI-generated, and with smaller-scale studies showing similar short-term gains but no long-term benefits.
While AI can support learning when used intentionally, overreliance may hinder the development of critical cognitive and social skills, according to research summaries.
The full study's findings have not yet been independently verified by other institutions.

headline_marked: Kagi Search [[Removes Paywalled Links]] from Results, Adds Stock Charts
headline: Kagi Search Removes Paywalled Links from Results, Adds Stock Charts
summary: The search engine Kagi now offers a setting to automatically filter out paywalled articles, alongside an enhanced Stocks widget featuring price charts and animations.
details: Kagi, a subscription-based search engine, has introduced a new feature allowing users to automatically remove paywalled links from their search results. This aims to provide users with direct access to content without encountering subscription barriers.

In addition to the paywall removal, Kagi has significantly updated its Stocks widget. The widget now displays information for exchange-traded funds (ETFs) and includes animated price charts that visually contextualize price fluctuations across different time windows.

The search engine also boasts improvements to user messages, which now render links, Markdown, and LaTeX for richer communication. Search functionality has been enhanced, allowing users to search across all threads and sort results by recency or alphabetically, with a new command to filter by folder.

Kagi is also offering more control over temporary threads, with options to retain them for 24 hours, 7 days, or 30 days. These updates are part of an effort to create a calmer and more user-friendly settings experience.
